es: Evaluar progreso y ajustar una estrategia sin abandonar la meta.
Resolver una tutoría de seguimiento con resultados parciales.

teaching.en: Review the evidence before you change your plan.

Keep practising beside the loud television.
Replace the listening goal with copying words.

feedback.es: El lugar tranquilo reduce el ruido y conserva la habilidad que se quiere mejorar.

origin.audio: Maya explains ideas clearly but misses final sounds. She records answers to hear mistakes. Her score rose from five to seven out of ten; her goal is nine. Evening noise interrupted two sessions. Her tutor recommends a quiet room. They agree to practise there on Tuesday and Thursday and compare recordings next Friday.

origin.text: Noah understands the main idea but gives answers without evidence. His tutor asks him to underline supporting lines. His score rose from two to three out of five; the target is four. Long texts prevent him finishing. They agree to use shorter texts and review four answers on Monday.

prompt.es: Caso B: revisa el plan en 90–120 palabras y justifica el ajuste.

answer.text: I identify the main idea well, but I need evidence for my answers. My score rose from two to three out of five, so my results have improved. My goal is still four supported answers out of five. Long texts take too much time. Following my tutor’s advice, I will use shorter texts and underline supporting lines to explain my answers. I will practise for fifteen minutes on Monday, Wednesday and Friday for two weeks. Next Monday, I will bring four answers with underlined lines so that we can check whether this change helps.

origin.audio: Iris, you identify the speaker well, but you miss numbers. Your tutor recommends pausing after each number and writing it down. Practise at lunch because you are too tired at night.

prompt.es: Caso C: escribe una revisión de 90–120 palabras con el próximo control.

answer.text: I identify speakers well, but I still miss numbers in voice messages. My score improved from four to six, although my goal remains eight details out of ten. I am too tired at night, so I will practise at lunch. Following my tutor’s advice, I will pause after each number and write it down to check what I hear. I will study for ten minutes on Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday for two weeks. I will keep dated answer sheets as evidence. On Saturday, we will compare the next sheet with the first one to review my progress.
